title: SIPP care and work constraints vary across race groups with uneven precision
source_unit: SIPP person record by reference month, stratified by released race recode, using final person and Fay-BRR replicate weights

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own race and conditional universe

observations.method: Official race status flag and child-care status flags/universes; WPFINWGT full estimate and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights with G=240 and perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals are design-based approximations; time lost is conditional on work prevention.
observations.counterinterpretation: Race recodes do not identify culture, discrimination, eligibility, provider access, or a causal mechanism.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own race and conditional universe

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method as the White-alone subgroup.
observations.uncertainty: Intervals are design-based approximations; payment and time-lost estimates are less precise than the work-prevention estimate.
observations.counterinterpretation: The descriptive contrast does not establish differences in care need, work opportunity, provider access, household composition, or treatment.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own race and conditional universe

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method; small cells are retained with intervals.
observations.uncertainty: Payment, work-prevention, and especially time-lost estimates are imprecise; intervals should not be used for fine ranking.
observations.counterinterpretation: The released race recode is not a cultural identity measure and does not identify care arrangements or institutional treatment.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each measure has its own race and conditional universe

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method; residual category and small time-lost cell are not ranked.
observations.uncertainty: All subgroup estimates are less precise than the White-alone estimates; time lost is especially unstable.
observations.subgroup: ERACE code 4: residual released race category.
observations.counterinterpretation: The residual category combines heterogeneous classifications and cannot support a substantive cultural interpretation.

related_sources.claim: Official race recode, status flags, child-care universes, and labels.

boundary: This is a person-weighted, design-based race-group comparison using a released recode. It does not establish culture, discrimination, causal care effects, household prevalence, provider access, recovery, trust, or political action.
